chunks: You may haply omit some of what has been revealed to you, and may be disheartened because they say: 'Why was no treasure sent down to him, or an angel accompanied him?' Yet you have been sent to warn alone, for God takes care of everything.
ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet feel disheartened and what was his role according to this verse?
ai.summary: In the context of the Meccan period, this verse comforts the Prophet (peace be upon him) against the psychological burden of the Quraysh's demands for tangible miracles, such as treasure or an accompanying angel, to validate his prophethood. Shia exegesis highlights that this reassurance underscores the sufficiency of the Quranic message itself, affirming that his role as a warner is complete without necessitating supernatural spectacles, while God remains the ultimate agent of all affairs.
